title: Robust spin pseudogap and spin-charge separation in the $σt$-$J$ model
authors: Zheng-Yuan Yue, Jia-Xin Zhang, Zheng-Cheng Gu
abstract: The $σt$-$J$ model, obtained from the usual $t$-$J$ model by flipping the sign of the spin-down hopping term, has been proposed to eliminate the strong interference between doped holes and the spin background, known as the phase string effect. In this work, we investigate the finite-temperature properties of the $σt$-$J$ model using infinite projected entangled-pair state (iPEPS) algorithms, in comparison with the $t$-$J$ model and its easy-plane variants. We show that these models share similar spin-pseudogap thermodynamics, with a maximum in the spin susceptibility at $T^* \sim J$ and a broad specific-heat peak. Tensor network renormalization (TNR) further provides strong evidences for a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition in the spin sector of the $σt$-$J$ model at a lower temperature $T_\text{BKT} < T^*$ due to its reduced $\mathrm{U}(1)$ spin-rotation symmetry. Crucially, in contrast to the $t$-$J$ model and to its easy-plane variants that also exhibit BKT transitions, these signatures remain robust upon doping: the doped holes preserve and even enhance the antiferromagnetic correlations in the $xy$ spin plane, leading to a weak doping dependence of both $T^*$ and $T_\text{BKT}$. Finally, we develop a slave-fermion mean-field theory for the $σt$-$J$ model, whose projective symmetry group (PSG) is selected based on numerically determined hopping and pairing correlations, and show that it explains the robust spin pseudogap upon doping.
summary: This work investigates the $\sigma t$-$J$ model to understand spin-charge dynamics in doped Mott insulators. Using advanced tensor network methods, the authors show that this modified model retains robust signatures of a spin pseudogap and BKT transition even when holes are introduced. This provides theoretical support for mechanisms preserving antiferromagnetic correlations crucial for unconventional superconductivity.
main_problem: The study investigates the interplay between spin and charge degrees of freedom, specifically addressing the pseudogap regime in doped Mott antiferromagnets.
main_result: The $\sigma t$-$J$ model exhibits robust signatures of a spin pseudogap and BKT transition upon doping, suggesting that altering the hole-spin coupling preserves key magnetic correlations found in cuprates.
method: The research employs advanced numerical techniques like infinite projected entangled-pair state (iPEPS) algorithms and Tensor Network Renormalization (TNR), supplemented by developing a slave-fermion mean-field theory.
model_or_system: The primary system is the $\sigma t$-$J$ model, a variant of the $t$-$J$ model where the sign of the spin-down hopping term is flipped to mitigate phase string effects. This modification reduces the spin rotation symmetry from SU(2) to U(1).
key_observables: Spin pseudogap thermodynamics (maximum in spin susceptibility at $T^* \sim J$), Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition temperature ($T_{BKT}$), and doping dependence of these features.
important_parameters: Doping ($\delta$), Temperature ($T$), Exchange coupling ($J$), Hopping parameter ($t$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on iPEPS/TNR methods for finite-temperature properties, and the mean-field theory constrains its Projective Symmetry Group (PSG) based on numerical results.
figures_summary: Not specified in detail, but notes reference comparisons between $\sigma t$-$J$ and $t$-$J$ models regarding pseudogap thermodynamics and BKT transitions.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the $\sigma t$-$J$ model as a modification of the standard $t$-$J$ model. It then uses iPEPS/TNR to calculate finite-temperature properties, demonstrating shared thermodynamic features with the $t$-$J$ model but crucially showing robustness upon doping. Finally, it develops and validates a slave-fermion mean-field theory.
why_interesting: The use of tensor networks (iPEPS/TNR) to study strongly correlated electron models like the $t$-$J$ model is highly relevant for understanding quantum magnetism and high-$T_c$ superconductivity, bridging numerical simulation with fundamental condensed matter physics.
